title: Liezi
altTitles: Taoist Teachings from the Book of Lieh-Tzü
dateDisplay: c. 4th century BCE, with later layers
author: liezi
attributionNote: The book is named for Lie Yukou, a shadowy figure of the fourth century BCE whom the Zhuangzi presents as a master of the Dao. The received text is a later compilation, probably assembled in the third or fourth century CE from older material; its eight books were edited and annotated by Zhang Zhan.
description: The Liezi is the third of the classical Daoist books: a collection of stories and arguments on cosmogony, the Yellow Emperor's dream journeys, the relativity of waking and dreaming, Confucius as a teacher of the Dao, the questions of Pang, effort and destiny, and causality. Its fables are among the most famous in Chinese literature, and its calm, sceptical voice extends the Zhuangzi's themes into a distinct metaphysics of change.
historicalContext: Zhang Zhan's fourth-century edition and commentary established the text, whose antiquity and authenticity have been debated since the Song. Lionel Giles translated this selection for the Wisdom of the East series in 1912. His seven books follow the eight-book recension but omit the seventh, the Yang Chu chapter, which he published separately as Yang Chu's Garden of Pleasure.
availabilityNote: Selected translation. The seven books Giles translated are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one book per chapter. The omitted Yang Chu book is a separate work in this library in the same translator's version; the eighth book, 'Explaining Conjunctions', is not in this edition. Giles's editorial note and introduction are not part of the work.
